scope: Read-only operation-mutex, shared poison, platform-lock and deterministic-test review.

findings.detail: The added supervisor operation mutex invalidates both old barrier schedules. In the waiter test, A holds operation while blocked in Sync; B waits on operation and never reaches beforeGate; the main goroutine waits for bWaiting before releasing A. In the unlock-window test, A holds operation while blocked inside Unlock; B waits for operation; the main goroutine waits for bResult before releasing A's unlockWait. Both cycles deterministically deadlock.
findings.required: Revise barriers around the new operation serialization. Signal B invocation without requiring entry into its OS lock, release A before awaiting B, and use bounded waits plus cleanup that always releases barriers and joins workers. To lock poison-before-Unlock independently, inspect shared health at the Unlock seam while A is still paused; do not require B to return before A releases operation.

passed: All public-to-this-module journal operations acquire shared health.operation before journal mutex and OS lock; create/open use the same operation domain. No reverse acquisition was found in these files.

Operation is retained until Unlock completes and any Unlock error poisons shared health. A sibling cannot pass admission during the unlock-result publication window. Explicit health and post-lock checks remain.
Windows/Unix lock wrappers keep per-wrapper serialization, release local gates on failed acquisition, and expose nonblocking OS contention probes without opening paths.

The revised child test reports an explicit unsuccessful TryLock while the parent holds the lock, then uses TCP control to request blocking acquisition. It no longer infers contention from a 150ms absence window.
nonblocking_followups: Child process cleanup still uses unbounded Wait after Kill in the defer and timeout branch. Normal completion is bounded, but total cleanup is not strictly bounded if termination fails; retain this limitation or add a bounded join and evidence-preserving cleanup policy.

TryLock uses a blocking local gate before the nonblocking OS probe. Current child usage has an uncontended local wrapper, so the test is valid; do not advertise this as a generally nonblocking same-wrapper API.
limitations: No tests/builds/services executed and no code modified.
No new implementation blocker found within the reviewed catalog slice. The two deterministic test deadlocks block running this test set as currently written.
OS process-death release, full verified-handle lifecycle and supervisor integration remain separate acceptance gates.
